title: Thai Green Curry
subtitle: Thai green curry with chicken and coconut milk
excerpt: Thailand's most fragrant curry: chicken simmered in a coconut milk broth seasoned with homemade or bought green curry paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar, with Thai basil, kaffir lime leaves, and fresh green chilli. Bright, herbaceous, and deeply aromatic.

recipe.sourceNotes: Thai green curry (kaeng khiao wan, literally sweet green curry) is one of the most internationally known Thai dishes and a standard of Thai restaurant menus worldwide. The green colour comes from green chillies and herbs (coriander root, lemongrass, galangal, kaffir lime peel) in the paste, which distinguishes it from the red curry that uses red chillies. In Thailand the curry is typically quite thin and soupy; the thick, reduced, restaurant-style version is an adaptation to Western tastes. The curry paste is made by pounding all the aromatics in a mortar — a process that takes 20 to 30 minutes and produces a far superior result to a food processor, which cannot achieve the same smooth emulsification. For speed, shop-bought green curry paste is used here; Mae Ploy and Mae Sri are widely considered the best available commercial brands.

content.text: Fry the curry paste in a little oil until fragrant and darkened before adding any liquid. This removes the raw edge from the paste. If using tinned coconut milk, spoon the thick cream from the top of an unshaken tin and use that to fry the paste. Never boil the curry hard once the coconut milk is in; a gentle simmer stops it splitting.

content.text: Spoon the thick coconut cream from the top of the unshaken tins into a wok over medium-high heat (or use the oil). Fry the curry paste in the cream for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly, until it is very fragrant and the oil begins to separate.

Add the chicken pieces and toss to coat in the paste for 2 minutes. Pour in the remaining coconut milk and add the lemongrass and kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 12 to 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.

Add the peas and cook for 2 minutes. Season with fish sauce and sugar. Taste: the curry should be balanced between the richness of the coconut, the heat of the paste, and the saltiness of the fish sauce. Finish with a squeeze of lime and scatter the Thai basil leaves over the top. Serve with jasmine rice.
